newsitem.title: USA: Chances dim for withdrawal of yield-burn plan-GFOA.
newsitem.headline: Chances dim for withdrawal of yield-burn plan-GFOA.

text.p: Chances that the Treasury Department will withdraw the controversial settlement offer it made to municipalities last year concerning "yield burning" are dimming, a key GFOA official said on Saturday.

Arthur Heilman, chairman of the Government Finance Officers Association's governmental debt committee, said muni groups have heard nothing from Treasury since a January 27 meeting on the issue with Donald Lubick, the department's assistant secretary for tax policy.

Groups had asked the administration to withdraw the yield burning "revenue procedure" and let the Securities and Exchange Commission recover Treasury losses through enforcement actions against broker-dealers.

"We have not received an answer," Heilman said. "But with the kinds of messages we are getting, it seems that Treasury is saying they cannot ignore violations of tax law," he said, during a briefing at GFOA's annual conference here.

Heilman noted that muni groups met with SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt in May 1997 and requested that SEC take the lead and coordinate its and the IRS' yield burning probes. Groups also asked that any penalties the SEC assesses broker-dealers be used to satisfy IRS settlements with issuers.
Levitt promised to get back to issuer groups in 30 to 60 days. "We are still waiting," Heilman said.

Heilman said SEC officials at the May meeting also raised agency concerns about political contributions in the muni bond arena. But issuer groups said "pay-to-play" and yield burning should be dealt with separately.
"We expressed concern that the yield-burning issue and pay-to-play should not be linked," Heilman said. "We don't think that is an appropriate link."
